subject: Civil Engineering
title: The Tacoma Narrows Collapse
description: Learn The Tacoma Narrows Collapse in one minute.

hook.text: On November 7, 1940, a bridge twisted itself apart in a 40 mph wind.

buildup.text: The Tacoma Narrows deck was too flexible. Wind set it oscillating like a ribbon.

discovery.text: Aeroelastic flutter — wind energy matched the bridge's natural frequency.

twist.text: Engineers had ignored aerodynamics. Bridges were designed for weight, not wind shape.

climax.text: After this failure, every suspension bridge was tested in wind tunnels first.

punchline.text: One collapsed bridge changed how every bridge is designed.

quiz.question: What caused the Tacoma Narrows Bridge to collapse?
options: Aeroelastic flutter — wind matched the bridge's natural frequency
The cables were too thin to support the deck weight

details.summary: The original Tacoma Narrows Bridge collapsed spectacularly on November 7, 1940, just four months after opening, when moderate 67 km/h winds induced violent torsional oscillations.
details.whyItMatters: The Tacoma Narrows collapse transformed bridge engineering by demonstrating that aerodynamic stability is as important as static strength. It launched the field of bridge aerodynamics that governs modern long-span bridge design.
takeaways: Aerodynamic instability, not resonance, caused the destructive torsional flutter
The shallow, solid plate-girder deck was vulnerable to wind-induced oscillation
Modern long-span bridges use aerodynamic deck shapes tested in wind tunnels

faq.question: Was the Tacoma Narrows collapse caused by resonance with the wind?
faq.answer: No. The common textbook explanation of resonance is incorrect. The failure was caused by aeroelastic flutter, a self-excited oscillation where the bridge deck's own motion changes the aerodynamic forces in a way that amplifies the motion further.

faq.question: How did the Tacoma Narrows failure change bridge design?
faq.answer: All long-span bridges now undergo wind tunnel testing with scale models and computational fluid dynamics analysis. Deck sections are designed with streamlined shapes that prevent flutter. Open truss decks replaced solid plate girders to reduce wind sensitivity.
